item.title: Uganda’s Nomination for UN Boss Is 30 Years and Many Months Late
item.description: Olara Otunnu was a prominent name in United Nations corridors. He was Uganda’s permanent representative in the 1980s. He led prestigious policy think tanks, such as the International Peace Institute, then known as International Peace Academy, in the ’90s. item.title: Cyprus: Guterres calls for renewed trust and a new meeting on the way forward
item.description: The United Nations Secretary-General said on Wednesday that he plans to convene fresh talks on Cyprus to resolve the decades-long division on the Mediterranean island, stressing that the moment calls for rebuilding trust between its two communities.

item.title: Hunger hampers Ebola response as cases top 3,200 in DR Congo
item.description: The UN emergency food agency appealed for immediate funding on Wednesday, warning that deepening hunger is undermining the response to an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) that has now infected more than 3,200 people.

item.title: UN warns West Bank settler violence hits ‘all-time high’ as calls grow to end occupation'
item.description: Violence in the occupied West Bank is worsening as the Israeli Government continues to approve new settlements, while settlers and Israeli security forces have “often” acted together to attack local Palestinian communities, the UN’s human rights office (OHCHR) warned on Wednesday.

item.title: The United Nations in a Time of Opportunity & Uncertainty: a Time to Choose
